purpose: Explain the 20x cap and test whether it is a theoretical boundary or a development-risk control. Uses burned A+B only; does not touch C/HOLDOUT or live outcomes.
common_rule: Candidate A and B1a agree top1; conservative top1 probability >=0.40; choose one 3renhuku ticket from consensus top3; conservative ticket EV >=10%; flat ¥100 per selected race.
interpretation: 20x is not a theoretical truth. It is a development-derived risk-control boundary.
The strongest two-sided burned A/B region is approximately 15x-20x. At 15x, A and B are both positive with 76 bets; at 20x, A and B are both positive with 89 bets.
Above 20x, A turns negative at 25x and worsens as the cap is relaxed, while B remains positive. This segment divergence is a warning that additional longshot exposure is unstable.
Removing the cap entirely leaves only +5% combined ROI while A is -20.3%; that is not acceptable evidence of stable edge.
Do not change the already-live 20x rule before tonight's outcomes. The 15x figure is diagnostic sensitivity, not a post-hoc replacement.

break_even_math.rule: For decimal odds O, true ticket probability p must satisfy p*O > 1 for positive expected return.
break_even_math.note: At high odds the break-even probability is tiny, so a small absolute probability overestimate can create a fake large EV. This is why tail calibration matters.
